\subsection{\texttt{seek}}
\label{ref:seek}
\icmd{seek}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{seek}
Moves an open managed file handle to a new position and returns the handle for continued piping.

\begin{signature}
seek [handle] <offset> [begin|current|end]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
handle & The managed file handle to reposition. (optional) \\
offset & The byte offset to seek to or by. \textit{(long)} \\
origin & The seek origin: begin, current, or end. Defaults to begin. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} record
 --- Consumes a piped file handle when no explicit handle argument is supplied.

\textbf{Output:} Moves the handle and returns it so you can continue piping into `read-from`, `read-line-from`, `read-to-end`, or `copy-to`.

\begin{lstlisting}
seek $handle 0 begin
$handle | seek 128 current
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
These commands work with managed file handles returned by `open-file` or by `FileSystemEntry` methods like `OpenText()` and `OpenRead()`. `seek` returns the handle so you can keep piping through the stream workflow, while `copy-to` copies from one compatible handle into another.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{stat}}
\label{ref:stat}
\icmd{stat}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{stat}
Returns detailed metadata for one or more paths.

\begin{signature}
stat [-L] [-f|--filesystem] [--show columns] [--hide columns] \\
\quad [--show-all] <path> [path...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path & One or more paths to inspect. \textit{(path-like)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-L & Dereference symlinks before reading metadata. \\
-f, --filesystem & Return filesystem usage information for the containing mount instead of file-entry metadata. \\
--show <columns> & Select which properties are rendered. \\
--hide <columns> & Hide specific properties from the output. \\
--show-all & Display every available column. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} list
 --- Uses piped path-like values when explicit paths are omitted.

\textbf{Output:} Typed filesystem-entry metadata, or filesystem-usage objects in -f mode.

\begin{lstlisting}
stat ./README.md
stat -L ./link.txt  # Dereference symlink
stat -f . | get { RequestedPath, FileSystem, MountedOn }  # Filesystem mode
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{tempfile}}
\label{ref:tempfile}
\icmd{tempfile}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{tempfile}
Creates a temporary file and returns it as a file system entry.

\begin{signature}
tempfile [prefix] [extension]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
prefix & Optional prefix for the file name. Defaults to 'tosh'. (optional) \\
extension & Optional file extension. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Returns a FileSystemEntry for the created temporary file.

\begin{lstlisting}
tempfile
tempfile data .csv  # Custom prefix and extension
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{touch}}
\label{ref:touch}
\icmd{touch}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{touch}
Creates files or updates access and modification timestamps.

\begin{signature}
touch [-acm] [-d time|-r file] [-c] <path> [path...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path ... & One or more filesystem paths to create or timestamp. \textit{(path-like)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-a & Update only the access time. \\
-m & Update only the modification time. \\
-c & Do not create missing files. \\
-d <time> & Use an explicit timestamp value. \\
-r <path> & Copy the timestamp from another file or directory. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} list
 --- Consumes piped path-like input when explicit paths are omitted.

\textbf{Output:} Returns updated FileInfo or DirectoryInfo objects for the paths it touched.

\begin{lstlisting}
touch notes.txt
touch -c -a notes.txt
touch -d 2026-03-28T12:00:00 notes.txt
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Touch now supports `-a`, `-m`, `-c`, `-d`, and `-r`, plus grouped short flags like `-am`.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{tree}}
\label{ref:tree}
\icmd{tree}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{tree}
Wraps the system tree utility, returning typed tree-entry objects.

\begin{signature}
tree [-adfL level] [--show columns] [--hide columns] [--show-all] [path \\
\quad ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path & Directory paths to tree. Defaults to current directory. (optional) \textit{(path-like)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-a & Include hidden files. \\
-d & List directories only. \\
-f & Print full path for each entry. \\
-L <level> & Limit recursion depth. \\
--show <columns> & Select which properties are rendered. \\
--hide <columns> & Hide specific properties from the output. \\
--show-all & Display every available column. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Returns typed tree-entry objects.

\begin{lstlisting}
tree
tree -L 2 -d  # Directories only, 2 levels
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{write-bytes}}
\label{ref:write-bytes}
\icmd{write-bytes}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{write-bytes}
Writes byte-oriented content to a file, replacing any previous contents.

\begin{signature}
write-bytes <path> [bytes...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path & The file path to create or replace. \textit{(path-like)} \\
bytes ... & Optional explicit byte-oriented values. When omitted, pipeline input becomes the byte payload. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- When no explicit byte values are supplied, pipeline input is converted into a byte payload.

\textbf{Output:} Returns the resulting filesystem entry for the written file.

\begin{lstlisting}
write-bytes ./data.bin [1, 2, 3, 255]
read-bytes ./source.bin | write-bytes ./copy.bin
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Write-bytes accepts raw byte arrays, byte-like collections, and byte-convertible scalar values. Strings are encoded as UTF-8 in this first slice.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{write-file}}
\label{ref:write-file}
\icmd{write-file}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{write-file}
Writes plain text to a file, replacing any previous contents.

\begin{signature}
write-file <path> [value...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path & The file path to create or replace. \textit{(path-like)} \\
value ... & Optional explicit text values to write. When omitted, pipeline input becomes the file body. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- When no explicit value arguments are supplied, pipeline values are rendered as plain text and written to the file.

\textbf{Output:} Returns the resulting filesystem entry for the written file.

\begin{lstlisting}
write-file ./notes.txt "hello world"
echo alpha beta | write-file ./notes.txt
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
These commands use ToSh's plain-text serialization rules, not the rich table renderer, so they are safe for intentional file output.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{write-line-to}}
\label{ref:write-line-to}
\icmd{write-line-to}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{write-line-to}
Writes one or more text lines to an open managed text file handle.

\begin{signature}
write-line-to <handle> [value...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
handle & The managed text file handle to write into. \\
value ... & Optional explicit values to write as one line. When omitted, each pipeline value becomes its own line. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- When no explicit values are supplied, each pipeline value is written as its own line.

\textbf{Output:} Writes line-oriented text into the handle and does not emit pipeline output.

\begin{lstlisting}
write-line-to $handle hello world
echo alpha beta | write-line-to $handle
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
These commands work with managed file handles returned by `open-file` or by `FileSystemEntry` methods like `OpenText()` and `OpenRead()`. `seek` returns the handle so you can keep piping through the stream workflow, while `copy-to` copies from one compatible handle into another.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{write-to}}
\label{ref:write-to}
\icmd{write-to}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Filesystem}}

\begin{cmdbox}{write-to}
Writes plain text or bytes to an open managed file handle.

\begin{signature}
write-to <handle> [value...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
handle & The managed file handle to write into. \\
value ... & Optional explicit values to write. When omitted, pipeline input becomes the written payload. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- When no explicit values are supplied, pipeline values are written into the handle.

\textbf{Output:} Writes into the handle and does not emit pipeline output.

\begin{lstlisting}
write-to $handle hello world
echo alpha beta | write-to $handle
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
These commands work with managed file handles returned by `open-file` or by `FileSystemEntry` methods like `OpenText()` and `OpenRead()`. `seek` returns the handle so you can keep piping through the stream workflow, while `copy-to` copies from one compatible handle into another.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}


\section{Functional}

\subsection{\texttt{compose}}
\label{ref:compose}
\icmd{compose}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{compose}
Composes two or more callables into a single callable that chains them left-to-right.

\begin{signature}
compose <callable1> <callable2> [callable ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable1 & The first callable in the chain. \\
callable2 & The second callable in the chain. \\
callable & Additional callables to chain. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} A single callable that applies all given callables in left-to-right order.

\begin{lstlisting}
compose func(x) => ($x + 1) func(x) => ($x * 2)  # Compose increment and double
$f = compose $parse $validate $transform; $f $input  # Build a processing pipeline
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{converge}}
\label{ref:converge}
\icmd{converge}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{converge}
Applies a callable to the seed repeatedly until two consecutive results are equal, then yields that stable value.

\begin{signature}
converge <seed> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seed & The initial value to start iterating from. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A function applied repeatedly until two consecutive results are equal. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} The first stable (fixed-point) value where consecutive applications produce equal results.

\begin{lstlisting}
converge 100 func(x) => ($x / 2 + 50 / $x)  # Newton's method for square root of 100
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{curry}}
\label{ref:curry}
\icmd{curry}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{curry}
Converts a fixed-arity callable into a curried callable value.

\begin{signature}
curry <callable>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable & A fixed-arity callable value to curry. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} none
 --- `curry` returns a callable that accumulates arguments until the original callable is saturated.

\textbf{Output:} Returns a curried callable. Calling it with too few arguments returns another callable; calling it with enough arguments runs the original callable.

\begin{lstlisting}
var add3 = func(a, b, c) => ($a + $b + $c); var curried = curry $add3  # Create a curried callable
var step1 = invoke $curried 1; var step2 = invoke $step1 2; invoke $step2 39  # Invoke a curried callable one step at a time
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{cycle}}
\label{ref:cycle}
\icmd{cycle}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{cycle}
Infinitely repeats the pipeline items in order.

\begin{signature}
... | cycle
\end{signature}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Items to repeat cyclically.

\textbf{Output:} The pipeline items repeated in order, infinitely.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | cycle | first 9  # Cycle a sequence
[a b c] | cycle | first 7  # Cycle an array
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Produces an infinite sequence. Always pair with `first`, `take-while`, or `take-until` to bound the output.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{invoke}}
\label{ref:invoke}
\icmd{invoke}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{invoke}
Invokes a callable value such as a lambda or function object.

\begin{signature}
invoke <callable> [arg ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable & A callable value such as an anonymous `func(...)` expression or other shell callable object. \\
arg ... & Optional positional arguments passed to the callable. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} none
 --- `invoke` is explicit-argument based for now. It does not automatically feed the current pipeline into the callable.

\textbf{Output:} Returns whatever values the callable yields.

\begin{lstlisting}
invoke (func(x) => ($x * 2)) 21  # Invoke an inline anonymous function
var add = func(x, y) => ($x + $y); invoke $add 3 4  # Store a lambda and invoke it later
var factor = 3; var scale = func(x) => ($x * $factor); invoke $scale 7  # Invoke a closure that captures lexical state
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{iterate}}
\label{ref:iterate}
\icmd{iterate}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{iterate}
Generates an infinite sequence by repeatedly applying a callable to the previous result, starting from a seed. Pair with 'take' or 'take-while' to bound the output.

\begin{signature}
iterate <seed> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seed & The initial value of the sequence. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A function applied to the previous value to produce the next. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} An infinite sequence: seed, f(seed), f(f(seed)), ...

\begin{lstlisting}
iterate 1 func(x) => ($x * 2) | first 10  # Powers of 2
iterate 0 { _ + 1 } | take-until { _ > 5 }  # Counting sequence bounded by take-until
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Produces an infinite sequence. Always pair with `first`, `take-until`, or `take-while` to bound the output.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{partial}}
\label{ref:partial}
\icmd{partial}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{partial}
Binds leading arguments to a callable and returns a new callable value.

\begin{signature}
partial <callable> [arg ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable & A callable value to partially apply. \\
arg ... & Leading positional arguments to bind ahead of time. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} none
 --- `partial` is explicit-argument based and returns a new callable value.

\textbf{Output:} Returns a callable value that prepends the bound arguments before invoking the original callable.

\begin{lstlisting}
var add = func(x, y) => ($x + $y); var inc = partial $add 1; invoke $inc 41  # Bind the first argument of a callable
invoke (partial (func(a, b, c) => ($"{$a}-{$b}-{$c}")) alpha beta) gamma  # Bind multiple leading arguments
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{recur}}
\label{ref:recur}
\icmd{recur}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{recur}
Generates an infinite sequence from seed values using a recurrence relation. The callable receives the last N values (matching seed count) and returns the next value.

\begin{signature}
recur <seeds> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seeds & The initial values of the recurrence, e.g. (0, 1) for Fibonacci. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A function applied to the last N values to produce the next. N matches the seed count. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} An infinite sequence: seeds..., f(seeds), f(seed[1..], f(seeds)), ...

\begin{lstlisting}
recur (0, 1) func(a, b) => ($a + $b) | first 10  # Fibonacci sequence
recur (1, 1, 1) func(a, b, c) => ($a + $b + $c) | first 10  # Tribonacci sequence
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Produces an infinite sequence. Always pair with `first`, `take-while`, or `take-until` to bound the output.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{repeat}}
\label{ref:repeat}
\icmd{repeat}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{repeat}
Produces a sequence of the same value repeated. Without a count argument, repeats infinitely.

\begin{signature}
repeat <value> [count]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
value & The value to repeat infinitely. \\
count & Optional maximum number of repetitions. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} The same value repeated.

\begin{lstlisting}
repeat 0 | first 5  # Five zeros
repeat hello 3  # Three hellos
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Without a count, produces an infinite sequence. Pair with `first`, `take-while`, or `take-until` to bound.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{repeatedly}}
\label{ref:repeatedly}
\icmd{repeatedly}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{repeatedly}
Produces an infinite sequence by re-evaluating a block for each item. The block receives the 0-based index.

\begin{signature}
repeatedly <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A block or function to evaluate each time. Receives the current index as \$\_ and as the first argument. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Infinite sequence of evaluated block results.

\begin{lstlisting}
repeatedly { random int 1 100 } | first 5  # Five random numbers
repeatedly func(i) => ($i * $i) | first 6  # Squares via index
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Produces an infinite sequence. Always pair with `first`, `take-while`, or `take-until` to bound the output.
\end{notebox}

\begin{notebox}
Unlike `repeat`, this re-evaluates the block for each item, so side effects and randomness work.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{unfold}}
\label{ref:unfold}
\icmd{unfold}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Functional}}

\begin{cmdbox}{unfold}
Generates values from a seed by repeatedly applying a callable. The callable receives the current state and must return a [value, next-state] pair, or null to stop.

\begin{signature}
unfold <seed> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seed & The initial state passed to the callable. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A function that receives state and returns [value, next-state] or null to stop. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} A sequence of values produced by the callable until it returns null.

\begin{lstlisting}
unfold 1 func(n) => if ($n <= 5) { [$n ($n + 1)] } else { null }  # Generate 1 through 5
unfold [0 1] func(s) => [($s[0]) [($s[1]) ($s[0] + $s[1])]]  # Fibonacci sequence
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}


\section{Math}

\subsection{\texttt{round}}
\label{ref:round}
\icmd{round}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Maths}}

\begin{cmdbox}{round}
Rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places.

\begin{signature}
round [value] [decimals]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
value-or-decimals & A number to round (with optional decimals), or just the decimal count when input is piped. \\
decimals & Number of decimal places to round to. Defaults to 0. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar
 --- Accepts a numeric value to round when only the decimal count is passed as an argument.

\textbf{Output:} The rounded value as a double.

\begin{lstlisting}
round 3.14159 2  # Round a literal to 2 decimal places
echo 3.14159 | round 2  # Round a piped value to 2 decimal places
echo 3.7 | round  # Round a piped value to nearest integer
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}


\section{Network}

\subsection{\texttt{http}}
\label{ref:http}
\icmd{http}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Net}}

\begin{cmdbox}{http}
Sends HTTP requests and returns structured response objects or decoded bodies.

\begin{signature}
http \\
\quad <get|\allowbreak post|\allowbreak put|\allowbreak patch|\allowbreak delete|\allowbreak head|\allowbreak options|\allowbreak request|\allowbreak send|\allowbreak serve|\allowbreak host|\allowbreak servers|\allowbreak stop> \\
\quad ...
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
<get|\allowbreak post|\allowbreak put|\allowbreak patch|\allowbreak delete|\allowbreak head|\allowbreak options> <url> & Send an HTTP request immediately. (optional) \\
request <method> <url> & Build an immutable HTTP request definition without sending it yet. (optional) \\
send [request] & Send an HttpRequestDefinition or HttpRequestMessage from an argument or the pipeline. (optional) \\
serve|\allowbreak host <dir> & Start a temporary HTTP file server rooted at a directory and return a live server handle. (optional) \\
servers & List open HTTP file server handles. (optional) \\
stop [handle|\allowbreak id ...] & Stop one or more HTTP file servers, or all of them when no target is provided. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
--header <name> <value> & Add a request header. Repeatable. \\
--json <value> & Serialize a value as JSON request content. \\
--body <text> & Send plain text request content. \\
--file <path> & Send request content from a file. \\
--form <record> & Send application/x-www-form-urlencoded content from a record-like value. \\
--content-type <value> & Override the request content type. \\
--timeout <duration> & Set the per-request timeout. \\
--bearer <token> & Add a Bearer authorization header. \\
--auth basic <user> <pass> & Add a Basic authorization header. \\
--follow |\allowbreak  --no-follow & Control redirect following for the request. \\
--as <response|\allowbreak json|\allowbreak text|\allowbreak bytes|\allowbreak lines> & Choose how the response should be materialized. \\
--out <path> & Write the raw response body bytes to a file. \\
--fail & Turn HTTP non-success status codes into diagnostics instead of returning a response object/body. \\
--browse & For `http serve`, render a lightweight browser page with directory listings and share metadata. \\
--upload & For `http serve`, accept uploads. Browser uploads and raw PUT/POST uploads are both supported. \\
--once & For `http serve`, close the server after the first handled request. \\
--bind <address> & Bind `http serve` to a specific address. \\
--lan & Bind `http serve` to all interfaces and advertise LAN-friendly share URLs for other devices. \\
--port <port> & Bind `http serve` to a specific port. Use `0` to request an ephemeral port. \\
--index <file> & Serve this index file for directories before directory listings. \\
--token <token> & Protect `http serve` with a fixed token. The returned ShareUrl includes it automatically. \\
--generate-token & Generate a random token for `http serve` and return it on the server handle. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar
 --- `http send` accepts a single HttpRequestDefinition or HttpRequestMessage from the pipeline.

\textbf{Output:} Returns either a structured HttpResponseInfo object or a decoded body, depending on `--as`. `http serve` returns live HttpFileServerHandle objects.

\begin{lstlisting}
http get https://example.com --as text  # Fetch a text response
http post https://example.com/api --json {| Name = "Toast" |} --as response  # Send JSON and keep the structured response
http request GET https://example.com | http send --as response  # Build then send a request object
http serve ./share --browse  # Start a temporary file server with a lightweight share page
http serve ./share --browse --lan  # Share a directory with other devices on the same network
http serve ./dropbox --upload --generate-token  # Start a temporary upload server with a generated access token
http servers | get { Id, ShareUrl, Upload }  # Inspect open temporary file servers
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
The native `http` builtin is object-first and backed by .NET HttpClient. Use `--as response` for a structured response object, or `--as json|text|bytes|lines` to project the body directly. `http serve <dir>` starts a temporary file server and returns a live server handle; `--browse`, `--upload`, `--token`, `--generate-token`, and `--lan` turn it into a lightweight cross-platform sharing tool. Use `http servers`, `http stop`, or `close` to manage it.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{ip}}
\label{ref:ip}
\icmd{ip}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Net}}

\begin{cmdbox}{ip}
Wraps the system ip utility, returning typed objects for supported JSON-backed subcommands.

\begin{signature}
ip \\
\quad [addr|\allowbreak link|\allowbreak route|\allowbreak neigh|\allowbreak rule|\allowbreak netns|\allowbreak tunnel|\allowbreak tuntap|\allowbreak vrf|\allowbreak maddr|\allowbreak mroute|\allowbreak token|\allowbreak ntable] \\
\quad [verb] [filter ...] | ip <other-subcommand ...>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
addr|\allowbreak address|\allowbreak a [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del|\allowbreak flush] [filter ...] & Query or mutate network addresses. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through to the system `ip`. (optional) \\
link|\allowbreak l [show|\allowbreak set] [filter ...] & Query or mutate network links. Queries return typed objects; mutations (set up/down, etc.) pass through. (optional) \\
route|\allowbreak r [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del|\allowbreak change|\allowbreak replace] [filter ...] & Query or mutate routing table entries. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
neigh|\allowbreak neighbour|\allowbreak n [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del|\allowbreak flush] [filter ...] & Query or mutate ARP/neighbor table. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
rule|\allowbreak ru [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del] [filter ...] & Query or mutate routing policy rules. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
netns [list|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del|\allowbreak exec ...] & Query or manage network namespaces. `list` returns typed objects; other operations pass through. (optional) \\
tunnel|\allowbreak tun [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del|\allowbreak change] [filter ...] & Query or mutate IP tunnels. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
tuntap|\allowbreak tap [show|\allowbreak add|\allowbreak del] [filter ...] & Query or mutate TUN/TAP devices. Queries return typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
vrf [show|\allowbreak exec ...] [filter ...] & Query VRF devices or execute commands in a VRF context. `show` returns typed objects; `exec` passes through. (optional) \\
maddr|\allowbreak maddress [show] [filter ...] & Query multicast addresses per interface. Returns typed objects. (optional) \\
mroute|\allowbreak mr [show] [filter ...] & Query multicast routing table entries. Returns typed objects. (optional) \\
token [list|\allowbreak set|\allowbreak del] [filter ...] & Query or mutate tokenized interface identifiers. `list` returns typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
ntable [show|\allowbreak change] [filter ...] & Query or mutate the neighbor table parameters. `show` returns typed objects; mutations pass through. (optional) \\
<other-subcommand ...> & Unsupported subcommands fall back to the system `ip` utility unchanged. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} none
 --- The structured `ip` builtin is explicit-arg-first and does not currently consume pipeline input.

\textbf{Output:} Query subcommands return typed objects (interfaces, routes, neighbors, rules, namespaces). Mutation subcommands (add, del, set, etc.) pass through to the system `ip` utility and return its text output.

\begin{lstlisting}
ip addr  # List interfaces as structured objects
ip link | where _.IsUp  # Filter active interfaces in the pipeline
ip route | where _.IsDefault  # Show the default route as a typed object
ip addr | each { _.Addresses } | flatten | get Address  # Project nested typed IP addresses
ip addr add 192.168.1.100/24 dev eth0  # Add an IP address to an interface
ip link set eth0 up  # Bring an interface up
ip route del default  # Delete the default route
ip netns  # List network namespaces as structured objects
ip tunnel  # List IP tunnels as structured objects
ip tuntap  # List TUN/TAP devices as structured objects
ip maddr  # List multicast addresses per interface
ip ntable  # Show neighbor table parameters
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
ToSh wraps `ip addr`, `ip link`, `ip route`, `ip neigh`, `ip rule`, `ip netns`, `ip tunnel`, `ip tuntap`, `ip vrf`, `ip maddr`, `ip mroute`, `ip token`, and `ip ntable` around the JSON-capable system utility so queries flow through the pipeline as typed objects. Mutation verbs (add, del, set, change, replace, flush) pass through to the system `ip` utility directly. Other subcommands fall back to the external `ip` utility unchanged.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{ping}}
\label{ref:ping}
\icmd{ping}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Net}}

\begin{cmdbox}{ping}
Pings a host and returns typed reply objects.

\begin{signature}
ping [-c count] [-W timeout-ms] [-s size] [-i interval] [-t ttl] [-4|-6] \\
\quad [-D] <host>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
host & Host name or IP address to ping. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-c, --count <count> & Number of echo requests to send. Defaults to 4. \\
-W, --timeout <milliseconds> & Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 4000. \\
-s, --size <bytes> & Payload size in bytes. Defaults to 32. \\
-i, --interval <seconds> & Delay between requests, in seconds. Defaults to 1. \\
-t, --ttl <hops> & Set the IP time-to-live value for requests. \\
-4 & Resolve and use an IPv4 address. \\
-6 & Resolve and use an IPv6 address. \\
-D, --dont-fragment & Set the don't-fragment flag where supported. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Per-reply records: address, round-trip time, and status flag.

\begin{lstlisting}
ping -c 3 localhost  # Ping localhost three times
ping -4 -W 1000 example.com | get { Host, Sequence, Status, RoundtripTime }  # Project typed ping replies
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}


\section{Pipeline}

\subsection{\texttt{all}}
\label{ref:all}
\icmd{all}

\begin{cmdbox}{all}
Returns true if every pipeline value matches the predicate.

\begin{signature}
all <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block predicate evaluated with ToastScript truthiness. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and stops at the first non-matching item.

\textbf{Output:} Returns `true` if every item matches the predicate; otherwise `false`.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 2 4 6 | all func(x) => ((($x % 2) == 0))  # Check whether all items match
ls | all { _.Exists }
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{any}}
\label{ref:any}
\icmd{any}

\begin{cmdbox}{any}
Returns true if any pipeline value matches the predicate.

\begin{signature}
any <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block predicate evaluated with ToastScript truthiness. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and stops at the first matching item.

\textbf{Output:} Returns `true` if any item matches the predicate; otherwise `false`.

\begin{lstlisting}
ps | any func(p) => ($p.Name == "sshd")
echo 1 2 3 | any func(x) => ($x == 2)  # Check whether any item matches
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{average}}
\label{ref:average}
\icmd{average}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{average}
Averages numeric, quantity, storage size, or timespan values.

\textit{Aliases:} \code{avg}

\begin{signature}
average [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract numeric values from each object. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the pipeline and returns the arithmetic mean.

\textbf{Output:} The arithmetic mean of the pipeline values. Supports numeric, Quantity, StorageSize, and TimeSpan types.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 10 20 30 | average  # Average a list of numbers
echo 1`km 500`m | average  # Average compatible quantities
ls | average .Length  # Average file sizes
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{cartesian-product}}
\label{ref:cartesian-product}
\icmd{cartesian-product}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{cartesian-product}
Produces the Cartesian product of two sequences. For infinite sources, uses diagonal enumeration.

\begin{signature}
... | cartesian-product <other-sequence> [callable|block]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
other-sequence & A second sequence to form pairs with. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & Optional combiner. Receives each pair as arguments. Defaults to [a, b] arrays. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- First sequence for the Cartesian product.

\textbf{Output:} All combinations of items from the pipeline and the other sequence.

\begin{lstlisting}
[1 2] | cartesian-product [a b]  # All pairs: [1,a],[1,b],[2,a],[2,b]
1.. | cartesian-product (1..) | first 10  # Diagonal enumeration of infinite sources
echo 1 2 3 | cartesian-product [10 20] func(a, b) => ($a * $b)  # With combiner
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
For infinite sources, uses diagonal (Cantor) enumeration so every pair is reached in finite time.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{chain}}
\label{ref:chain}
\icmd{chain}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{chain}
Lazily concatenates the pipeline with one or more sequences.

\begin{signature}
... | chain <sequence> [sequence ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
sequences & One or more arrays, lists, or ranges to concatenate after the pipeline. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Pipeline items are yielded first, followed by each argument sequence.

\textbf{Output:} All items from the pipeline (if any) followed by all items from each argument sequence.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 | chain [3 4] [5 6]  # Concatenate multiple sequences
echo a b c | chain [d e f]  # Append to pipeline
chain [1 2] [3 4] [5 6]  # Concatenate without pipeline input
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{chunk}}
\label{ref:chunk}
\icmd{chunk}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{chunk}
Groups pipeline items into fixed-size batches.

\begin{signature}
chunk <size>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
size & The number of items per chunk. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Collects pipeline items into fixed-size batches.

\textbf{Output:} Arrays of up to `size` items. The last chunk may be smaller.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 5 | chunk 2  # Group into pairs
1..10 | chunk 3 | map { count }  # Chunk then count each group
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{collect}}
\label{ref:collect}
\icmd{collect}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{collect}
Collects all pipeline items into a single list.

\begin{signature}
collect
\end{signature}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record, list, table
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and buffers every incoming item into one array result.

\textbf{Output:} Returns a single array containing the pipeline items in order.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | collect  # Collect scalar pipeline items into one array
ls *.cs | collect  # Capture a multi-item file listing as one value
findmnt -l | where _.FsType == ext4 | collect  # Buffer filtered structured rows into one array
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{combinations}}
\label{ref:combinations}
\icmd{combinations}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{combinations}
Yields all k-element combinations (subsets) of the pipeline items.

\begin{signature}
... | combinations <k>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
k & The number of elements in each combination. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Items to select combinations from.

\textbf{Output:} Arrays of k elements from the pipeline in lexicographic order.

\begin{lstlisting}
[1 2 3] | combinations 2  # All 2-element subsets
echo a b c d | combinations 3  # All 3-element subsets
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{count}}
\label{ref:count}
\icmd{count}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{count}
Counts the number of objects in the current pipeline.

\begin{signature}
count
\end{signature}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the entire pipeline and returns the count.

\textbf{Output:} An integer representing the total number of pipeline objects.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo a b c | count  # Count items in a pipeline
ls | count  # Count files in the current directory
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{dedup}}
\label{ref:dedup}
\icmd{dedup}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{dedup}
Removes consecutive duplicate values from the pipeline. Unlike 'distinct', preserves non-adjacent duplicates.

\begin{signature}
... | dedup [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract the comparison key from each object. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Yields each item only if different from the previous.

\textbf{Output:} Pipeline items with consecutive duplicate values removed.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 1 2 2 3 1 1 | dedup  # Remove consecutive duplicates
ls | sort-by .Extension | dedup .Extension  # Dedup by member path
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Unlike `distinct`, only removes adjacent duplicates. Preserves non-consecutive repeats.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{describe}}
\label{ref:describe}
\icmd{describe}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{describe}
Returns descriptive statistics for numeric pipeline values.

\begin{signature}
describe [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract numeric values from each object. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the pipeline and returns descriptive statistics.

\textbf{Output:} A table of summary statistics: Count, Mean, Median, StdDev, Min, Max, Q1, Q3.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 23 45 12 67 34 89 11 55 | describe  # Summary statistics
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{distinct}}
\label{ref:distinct}
\icmd{distinct}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{distinct}
Removes duplicate pipeline values.

\begin{signature}
distinct [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract the comparison key from each object. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Yields each pipeline object only the first time its value (or keyed value) is seen.

\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{each}}
\label{ref:each}
\icmd{each}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{each}
Executes a block or callable once for each input object.

\textit{Aliases:} \code{foreach}

\begin{signature}
each <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block executed once per input item. \\
\bottomrule

 --- Consumes the current pipeline and executes the callable or block once per input item.

\textbf{Output:} Returns whatever values the callable or block emits for each input item.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo one two | each { _.ToUpper() }  # Transform each item to uppercase
DriveInfo.GetDrives() | each func(d) => ($d.Name)  # Extract drive names
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Collections stay intact until you explicitly expand them with `each` or `flatten`.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{enumerate}}
\label{ref:enumerate}
\icmd{enumerate}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{enumerate}
Pairs each pipeline item with its index, yielding [index, item] arrays.

\begin{signature}
... | enumerate [start]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
start & Optional starting index (default: 0). (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

 --- Each item is paired with its index.

\textbf{Output:} Two-element arrays [index, item] for each pipeline item.

echo a b c | enumerate 1  # 1-based indexing
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{\texttt{filter}}
\label{ref:filter}
\icmd{filter}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{filter}
Filters pipeline values with a callable value or block predicate.

\begin{signature}
filter <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block predicate evaluated with ToastScript truthiness. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and keeps only items whose predicate is truthy. Tree-shaped inputs are pruned like `where`.

\textbf{Output:} Returns the input items that matched the predicate.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 | filter func(x) => ((($x % 2) == 0))  # Filter with a lambda
ls | filter { _.Type == file }  # Filter with a block
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{find-index}}
\label{ref:find-index}
\icmd{find-index}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{find-index}
Returns the 0-based index of the first pipeline value matching the predicate, or -1 if none match.

\begin{signature}
find-index <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & Predicate callable or block evaluated for each pipeline value. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} An int — the zero-based index of the first matching item, or -1 if none matches.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 10 20 30 | find-index { _ == 20 }  # Find the first matching index
ls | find-index func(f) => $f.Name.EndsWith(".slnx")  # Find an index with a lambda
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{\texttt{first}}
\label{ref:first}
\icmd{first}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{first}
Returns the first object or first N objects from the pipeline.

\begin{signature}
first [count]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
count & The number of objects to return. Defaults to 1. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Yields the first N items then stops consuming.

\textbf{Output:} The first N pipeline objects.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | first  # Get the first item
ls | first 5  # Get the first five items
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{flat-map}}
\label{ref:flat-map}
\icmd{flat-map}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{flat-map}
Transforms each pipeline value with a callable or block then flattens the results.

\begin{signature}
flat-map <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A transform that returns a sequence for each input item. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Transforms each item and flattens the resulting sequences into one stream.

\textbf{Output:} The flattened results of applying the transform to each pipeline item.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | flat-map { [_ (_ * 10)] }  # Expand each item into two
ls | flat-map { ls $_.FullName }  # List contents of each subdirectory
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{flatten}}
\label{ref:flatten}
\icmd{flatten}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{flatten}
Explicitly expands enumerable pipeline values by one level.

\begin{signature}
flatten
\end{signature}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, list
 --- Expands each enumerable in the pipeline by one level.

\textbf{Output:} Individual items from each expanded enumerable in the pipeline.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo [1 2] [3 4] | flatten  # Flatten nested arrays
ls /tmp /var | flatten  # Flatten directory listings into one stream
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{frequencies}}
\label{ref:frequencies}
\icmd{frequencies}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{frequencies}
Counts occurrences of each distinct value in the pipeline.

\begin{signature}
frequencies [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to count frequencies of, instead of the whole item. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Records of the form \{ Value, Count \} describing how often each distinct input value occurred.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo red blue red green blue red | frequencies  # Count distinct values
ls | frequencies Extension  # Count file extensions
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{get}}
\label{ref:get}
\icmd{get}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{get}
Gets a member or projects fields from each pipeline item.

\textit{Aliases:} \code{pick}, \code{select}

\begin{signature}
get <member-path> or get <m1> <m2> ... or get \{ <member-path>, ... \}
\end{signature}

\textbf{Output:} The selected member value(s) — one item per requested path, in input order.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls -la | get Name  # Pluck a single field
ls | get Name Size Modified  # Project multiple fields (variadic)
ps | get { Name, PID, Memory }  # Project multiple fields with brace syntax
echo 1 2 3 | get func(x) => ($x * 2)  # Project with a function
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
`get` is the column-picker (member values). For row picking by index/range/list, use `row`.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{group-by}}
\label{ref:group-by}
\icmd{group-by}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{group-by}
Groups pipeline values by a member path, block, or callable.

\begin{signature}
group-by <member-path|callable|block>
\end{signature}

\textbf{Output:} Group records of the form \{ Key, Items \} — one per distinct key produced by the projection.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls | group-by Extension
ps | group-by func(p) => ($p.Name.Substring(0, 1))
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{group-while}}
\label{ref:group-while}
\icmd{group-while}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{group-while}
Groups consecutive items while the predicate holds.

\begin{signature}
group-while <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A predicate that receives each item. A new group starts when its result is falsy. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Groups consecutive pipeline items while the predicate is truthy.

\textbf{Output:} Arrays of consecutive items grouped while the predicate holds.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 1 2 2 3 | group-while { _ == $prev }  # Group equal consecutive values
echo 1 2 3 10 11 12 | group-while func(x, prev) => ($x - $prev <= 1)  # Group runs of nearly consecutive numbers
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{ignore}}
\label{ref:ignore}
\icmd{ignore}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{ignore}
Consumes and discards all pipeline input.

\begin{signature}
... | ignore
\end{signature}

\textbf{Output:} Emits nothing; drains the input pipeline silently.

\begin{lstlisting}
build-project | ignore  # Run for side effects and discard output
http post https://example.com/hooks --json $payload | ignore  # Suppress response output
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{inspect}}
\label{ref:inspect}
\icmd{inspect}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{inspect}
Inspects piped CLR objects inline, or returns legacy flat output with --flat.

\begin{signature}
inspect [-a] [--flat]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-a & Include non-public and static members in the inspection. \\
--flat & Use flat text output instead of the interactive tree browser. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Inspects each piped object.

\textbf{Output:} An interactive tree view or flat member-value records depending on mode.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls -la | first | inspect  # Inspect a file entry interactively
new System.Random() | inspect -a  # Inspect all members including private
new System.Random() | inspect --flat  # Flat output for scripting
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{notebox}
Inspect opens an inline tree browser for CLR values in interactive sessions. Use `-a` for non-public/static members, `--flat` for the legacy static inspection object output, and `i` inside the browser to insert the selected member text into the active REPL line at the cursor (or queue it for the next prompt when no line is active). In the REPL, `F2` tries to inspect the reference under the cursor, and `Alt+I` is available as a fallback on terminals that do not expose function keys cleanly.
\end{notebox}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{interleave}}
\label{ref:interleave}
\icmd{interleave}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{interleave}
Alternates items from the pipeline with items from another sequence.

\begin{signature}
interleave <other-sequence>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
other-sequence & An array or list to alternate with the pipeline items. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Alternates items from the pipeline with the other sequence.

\textbf{Output:} Items from the pipeline and the other sequence in alternating order.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | interleave [a b c]  # Alternate numbers and letters
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{intersperse}}
\label{ref:intersperse}
\icmd{intersperse}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{intersperse}
Inserts a separator value between each pair of pipeline items.

\begin{signature}
... | intersperse <separator>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
separator & The value to insert between each pipeline item. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Items are yielded with the separator between each pair.

\textbf{Output:} The original items with the separator inserted between each pair.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | intersperse 0  # Insert zeros between items
echo a b c | intersperse "-"  # Insert dashes
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{join}}
\label{ref:join}
\icmd{join}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{join}
Joins pipeline items into a single string, or combines path segments with -p/--path.

\begin{signature}
... | join [-p|--path] [separator-or-segment ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
separator-or-segment & In default mode: the string placed between items. In path mode (-p/--path): an additional path segment appended after any piped input. (optional) \textit{(string)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-p & Path mode: join segments with the platform path separator using System.IO.Path.Join semantics. Piped input is prepended; positional args are additional segments. \\
--path & Alias for -p. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record, list, table
 --- Consumes every pipeline item, converts it to a string, and joins them. In path mode, piped items become the leading path segments.

\textbf{Output:} Default mode: a single string of pipeline items separated by the given separator. Path mode: a single path string.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo a b c | join "-"  # Join scalar items with '-'
[1, 2, 3] | join ", "  # Stringify and join array elements
cat words.txt | lines | join " "  # Collapse lines into a single space-separated string
join -p "etc" "tosh" "config.toml"  # Build a path from arguments
pwd | join -p "logs" "today.log"  # Build a path from piped input plus more segments
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{last}}
\label{ref:last}
\icmd{last}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{last}
Returns the last object or last N objects from the pipeline.

\begin{signature}
last [count]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
count & The number of objects to return from the end. Defaults to 1. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Buffers the pipeline and returns the final N items.

\textbf{Output:} The last N pipeline objects.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | last  # Get the last item
ls | last 3  # Get the last three items
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\icmd{map}

map <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\

callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block that transforms each input item into exactly one output value. \\

 --- Consumes the current pipeline and emits one transformed value per input item.

\subsection{\texttt{none}}
\label{ref:none}
\icmd{none}

\begin{cmdbox}{none}
Returns true if no pipeline values match the predicate.

none <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\

callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block predicate evaluated with ToastScript truthiness. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and stops at the first matching item.

\textbf{Output:} Returns `true` if no items match the predicate; otherwise `false`.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | none func(x) => ($x > 10)  # Check whether no items match
ls | none { _.Type == link }
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{parallel}}
\label{ref:parallel}
\icmd{parallel}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{parallel}
Executes a block or callable concurrently for each input object.

\begin{signature}
parallel [--threads <n>] <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\

callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block executed once per input item, concurrently. \\
\bottomrule

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
--threads <n> & Maximum degree of parallelism (default: processor count). \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline and executes the callable or block in parallel for each input item.

\textbf{Output:} Returns whatever values the callable or block emits for each input item, in input order.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | parallel { echo (_ * 2) }  # Double each item in parallel
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{partition}}
\label{ref:partition}
\icmd{partition}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{partition}
Splits pipeline values into two lists based on a predicate: [matches, non-matches].

\begin{signature}
partition <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
callable|\allowbreak block & A predicate evaluated for each item using ToastScript truthiness. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the pipeline and splits items into two groups by predicate.

\textbf{Output:} A two-element array: [items-where-true, items-where-false].

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 5 | partition { _ > 3 }  # Partition by a condition
ls | partition { _.Extension == ".cs" }  # Separate C# files from others
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{reduce}}
\label{ref:reduce}
\icmd{reduce}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{reduce}
Folds the current pipeline into one value using a seed and callable value or block.

\begin{signature}
reduce <seed> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seed & The initial accumulator value. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A lambda or block that combines the current accumulator with each input item and returns the next accumulator. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the current pipeline from left to right and folds it into one final value.

\textbf{Output:} Returns the final accumulator value. On an empty input stream, `reduce` returns the seed unchanged.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 | reduce 0 func(acc, x) => ($acc + $x)  # Fold numeric values
echo one two three | reduce "" { $acc + _.Substring(0, 1) }  # Fold with a block
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{rename}}
\label{ref:rename}
\icmd{rename}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{signature}

\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
old new ... & One or more old/new field-name pairs to apply to each record-like input value. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Output:} Records describing each rename operation, or nothing when used purely for its side effect.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls | get { Name, Length } | rename Length Size  # Rename one field
ps | get { Id, Name } | rename Id Pid Name Command  # Rename several fields
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{reverse}}
\label{ref:reverse}
\icmd{reverse}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

Reverses the order of the current pipeline objects.

\begin{signature}
reverse

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Buffers the pipeline then yields items in reverse order.

\textbf{Output:} All pipeline objects in reversed order.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 | reverse  # Reverse a sequence
ls | sort .Name | reverse  # Reverse a sorted listing
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{row}}
\label{ref:row}
\icmd{row}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{row}
Picks one or more rows from the pipeline by index, range, or list of indices.

\begin{signature}
row <index ...> | row <range> | row <list>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
indices & One or more zero-based indices, a range, or a list/array of indices. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Reads input items by their zero-based position.

\textbf{Output:} The pipeline rows at the requested indices, in the order they were requested.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls | row 3  # Pick the row at index 3
ls | row 7 8 9  # Pick multiple rows by index (variadic)
ls | row [3, 1, 0]  # Pick rows from a list literal (preserves the listed order)
ls | row 2..5  # Pick a contiguous slice
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{scan}}
\label{ref:scan}
\icmd{scan}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{scan}
Like reduce but yields every intermediate accumulator value.

scan <seed> <callable|block>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
seed & The initial accumulator value. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & A function that takes (accumulator, current-item) and returns the new accumulator. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Folds the pipeline from left to right, yielding each intermediate value.

\textbf{Output:} Every intermediate accumulator value (one per input item).

\begin{lstlisting}

echo a b c | scan "" { $acc + _ }  # Running string concatenation
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{skip}}
\label{ref:skip}
\icmd{skip}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{skip}
Skips the first object or first N objects from the pipeline.

\begin{signature}
skip [count]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
count & The number of objects to skip. Defaults to 1. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes and discards the first N items, then yields the rest.

\textbf{Output:} The remaining pipeline objects after skipping the first N.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 5 | skip 2  # Skip the first two items
echo a b c | skip  # Skip the first item
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{skip-until}}
\label{ref:skip-until}
\icmd{skip-until}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{skip-until}
Skips input values until the predicate becomes true.

\begin{signature}
skip-until <predicate-expression|callable>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
predicate & A callable or block evaluated for each item. Starts yielding when its result is truthy. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Discards items until the predicate is truthy, then yields the rest.

\textbf{Output:} Pipeline items starting from the first that satisfies the predicate.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 5 | skip-until { _ >= 3 }  # Skip until a condition is met
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{skip-while}}
\label{ref:skip-while}
\icmd{skip-while}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{skip-while}
Skips input values while the predicate remains true.

\begin{signature}
skip-while <predicate-expression|callable>
\end{signature}

\textbf{Output:} All input items starting from (and including) the first one for which the predicate result was falsy.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 | skip-while { _ < 3 }
echo 1 2 3 4 | skip-while func(x) => ($x < 3)
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{sort}}
\label{ref:sort}
\icmd{sort}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{sort}
Sorts the current pipeline objects.

\textit{Aliases:} \code{sort-by}

\begin{signature}
sort [-r|--reverse] [-n|--numeric] [-u|--unique] [-h|--human-numeric] \\
\quad [-i|--ignore-case] [-o|--ordinal] [member-path|callable|block]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
key & A member path, callable, or block to extract the sort key. (optional) \textit{(member-path|callable|block)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-r, --reverse & Reverse the sort order. \\
-d, --desc, --descending & Alias for --reverse: sort in descending order. \\
-n, --numeric & Use numeric comparison. \\
-u, --unique & Remove duplicate values after sorting. \\
-h, --human-numeric & Human-numeric sort (understands storage sizes). \\
-i, --ignore-case & Order letters without regard to case. \\
-o, --ordinal & Compare by code point, case-sensitively. This is the default; accepted so existing scripts keep working. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar
 --- Collects all pipeline objects, sorts them, then re-emits.

\textbf{Output:} The input pipeline objects in sorted order.

\begin{lstlisting}
ps | sort Memory  # Sort by property
ls -la | sort Modified | reverse  # Sort then reverse
ps | sort func(p) => ($p.Name.Length)  # Lambda sort key
$names | sort -i  # Case-insensitive order, for reading
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract numeric values from each object. (optional) \\

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the pipeline and returns the standard deviation.

\textbf{Output:} The population standard deviation of the pipeline values.

\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

... | step-by <n>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
n & Take every Nth item (must be >= 1). \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

 --- Yields every Nth item from the pipeline.

1.. | step-by 3 | first 5  # Every 3rd integer
echo a b c d e f g | step-by 2  # Every other item

\subsection{\texttt{sum}}
\label{ref:sum}
\icmd{sum}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{sum}
Sums numeric, quantity, storage size, or timespan values.

\begin{signature}
sum [member-path]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
member-path & Optional member path to extract numeric values from each object. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Consumes the pipeline and returns the total.

\textbf{Output:} The sum of the pipeline values. Supports numeric, Quantity, StorageSize, and TimeSpan types.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 | sum  # Sum a list of numbers
echo 1`km 500`m | sum  # Sum compatible quantities
ls | sum .Length  # Total file sizes
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{\texttt{summarize}}
\label{ref:summarize}
\icmd{summarize}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{summarize}
Computes structured summary objects for requested aggregates over the pipeline.

\textit{Aliases:} \code{summary}

\begin{signature}
summarize [--sum [columns]] [--avg [columns]] [--min [columns]] [--max \\
\quad [columns]] [--count [columns]]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
{}[column|\allowbreak member-path] [--sum [columns]] [--avg [columns]] [--min [columns]] [--max [columns]] [--count [columns]] & With no arguments, infer every sensible aggregate for every summarizable column. A single bare column or member path such as `Size` or `\_.Used` narrows auto mode to that one target. Flags request explicit operations. (optional) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
--sum [columns] & Compute sums for scalar input or the named columns. \\
--avg [columns], --average [columns] & Compute averages for scalar input or the named columns. \\
--min [columns] & Compute minima for scalar input or the named columns. \\
--max [columns] & Compute maxima for scalar input or the named columns. \\
--count [columns] & Count input rows when no columns are supplied, or non-null values for the named columns. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record, list, table
 --- Consumes the current pipeline rows and returns one structured ColumnSummary object per requested or inferred scalar target or member path.

\textbf{Output:} Returns ColumnSummary objects describing the requested or inferred aggregates. The original input rows are not appended back into the result.

\begin{lstlisting}
df | summarize  # Infer every sensible aggregate for every summarizable df column
df | summarize _.Used  # Infer every sensible aggregate for a single member path target
seq 5 | summarize --sum --avg --min --max --count  # Summarize a scalar numeric pipeline explicitly
ps | summarize --avg Memory --max Memory  # Compute multiple aggregates over one column
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\label{ref:take-until}
\icmd{take-until}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{take-until}
Yields input values until the predicate becomes true.

\begin{signature}
take-until <predicate-expression|callable>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
predicate & A callable or block evaluated for each item. Stops when its result is truthy. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\textbf{Pipeline input:} scalar, record
 --- Yields items until the predicate is truthy.

\textbf{Output:} Pipeline items up to (but not including) the first that satisfies the predicate.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 5 | take-until { _ >= 4 }  # Take until a condition is met
1..100 | take-until func(x) => ($x > 10)  # Take until value exceeds 10
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{take-while}}
\label{ref:take-while}
\icmd{take-while}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{take-while}
Yields input values while the predicate remains true.

\begin{signature}
take-while <predicate-expression|callable>
\end{signature}

\textbf{Output:} Input items from the front of the stream up to (but not including) the first one for which the predicate result was falsy.

\begin{lstlisting}
echo 1 2 3 4 | take-while { _ < 3 }
echo 1 2 3 4 | take-while func(x) => ($x < 3)
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

\subsection{\texttt{tee}}
\label{ref:tee}
\icmd{tee}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{tee}
Passes values through while also writing them out or capturing them.

\begin{signature}
tee [-a] [path] or tee -v <name>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
path & Optional file path to write a copy of the stream to. (optional) \textit{(path-like)} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Flag / Option} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
-a, --append & Append to the output file instead of replacing it. \\
-v, --variable <name> & Capture the stream into a shell variable while still passing values through. \\
\bottomrule

\textbf{Output:} Re-emits each input item unchanged, while also writing it to the configured destination as a side effect.

\begin{lstlisting}
ls | tee snapshot.txt | where _.IsDirectory  # Write a copy to a file and keep piping
ps | tee -v processes | count  # Capture a pipeline into a variable
\end{lstlisting}

\end{cmdbox}

 --- Consumes the pipeline and returns the variance.

\subsection{\texttt{where}}
\label{ref:where}
\icmd{where}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{where}
Filters pipeline objects with a predicate block or callable.

\begin{signature}
where <predicate-expression|callable>
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
predicate & A predicate block or callable evaluated with ToastScript truthiness. \textit{(block|callable)} \\
\bottomrule

 --- Consumes any pipeline objects and tests each against the predicate.

ls -la | where func(item) => ($item.Name.ToLower().EndsWith(".md"))  # Lambda predicate

Inside predicate expressions, bare member access resolves against the current pipeline object.

\subsection{\texttt{window}}
\label{ref:window}
\icmd{window}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{window}
Yields sliding windows of a given size over the pipeline.

\begin{signature}
window <size> [callable|block]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\

size & The number of items in each sliding window. \\
callable|\allowbreak block & Optional transform applied to each window. (optional) \\

\end{tabular}

 --- Yields overlapping windows of the specified size as the pipeline flows.

\textbf{Output:} Arrays (or transformed results) for each sliding window position.

\begin{lstlisting}

1..10 | window 2 func(a, b) => ($a + $b)  # Pairwise sums

\subsection{\texttt{xargs}}
\label{ref:xargs}
\icmd{xargs}

\textit{Library: \code{Tosh.Stdlib.Pipeline}}

\begin{cmdbox}{xargs}
Builds command invocations from text input.

\begin{signature}
xargs [-n count] <command> [fixed-arg ...]
\end{signature}

\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\ttfamily\small\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{5cm} L{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Argument} & \textbf{Description} \\
\midrule
command & Command to invoke for the generated arguments. \\
fixed-arg ... & Arguments that are always passed before piped arguments. (optional) \\
